findings.title: HyperCore sends unsigned transfers in the name of addresses that never signed, including a contract, and the record that names such an address is outside the deployer's documented action
findings.difference: HyperCore places unsigned system transactions at the head of HyperEVM blocks and states their sender itself. The official endpoint shows them with r=0 and s=0, nanoreth encodes the sender in s. On Ethereum a balance leaves an address only through a transaction that address signed or a call made by its own code.
findings.mechanism: In a census of 5,405 blocks, 191 system transactions have sender 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00, an address without code, and 488 have sender 0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24, the USDC linked contract (2,175 byte proxy), each calling USDC transfer to the other. This matches the AQAv2 rebalance between a treasury address and the linked contract. If HyperCore recorded the PoolManager as such an address, a transfer in its name would lower the PoolManager's token balance while pool state, ERC-6909 balances and protocol fee counters still count it as owed, because the PoolManager compares balances only between sync and settle in one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, :349-365). Later takes in that token would revert inside the transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40-88).
findings.impact: All pools and ERC-6909 claims in a token for which HyperCore named the PoolManager as rebalancing address. Nothing is exposed today: the PoolManager nonce is 1 on all three endpoints read, and no gas price 0 transaction moves a token out of it.
findings.preconditions: Two staked deployers and a validator vote must name the PoolManager as treasury address. An ordinary account cannot.
findings.mitigations: Watch the PoolManager nonce on a nanoreth replica, which rises with any system transaction in its name. Ask the Hyperliquid team whether HyperCore refuses an address with code as AQAv2 treasury.

sources.supports: fetched 2026-11-26: the treasury deployer designates the treasury address; the linked contract rebalances with it at 9:1; activation by validator vote.
fetched 2026-11-26: authorizeAqav2Role takes token and role only; no documented action sets the treasury address.

sources.url: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com eth_getBlockByNumber over 5,405 census blocks and https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber over 150 of them, 2026-11-26
sources.supports: 191 system transactions from 0xc20699... and 488 from 0x6b9e77..., each calling USDC 0xb88339... transfer to the other; official eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber agrees on 150 blocks (raw/syscount.json).
No system transaction has used the PoolManager as sender (also 0x1 on rpc.hyperlend.finance and rpc.purroofgroup.com).
System transaction sender decoded from s with no signature check (lines 50-58, 77-97, 182-184).

cleared.check: L-994 twin state: every PoolManager storage slot that the logs show was ever written (whole history, 5,570 logs from deployment block 45,998,366 to 52,275,542: 414 Initialize, 2,284 Swap, 846 ModifyLiquidity, 2,023 ERC-6909 Transfer, 2 OperatorSet), the native balance and balanceOf(PoolManager) of all 316 pooled ERC-20 currencies, read on the official endpoint (validator state) and on two nanoreth replicas at the same block.
cleared.result: 8,464 slots were derived from the source layout (owner slot 0, protocolFeesAccrued 1, protocolFeeController 2, isOperator 3, balanceOf 4, allowance 5, _pools 6, Pool.State +0..+6, TickInfo and Position.State 3 words each, bitmap key sar(8, compressed)): 1,656 pool words, 3,240 tick words, 2,277 position words, 934 bitmap words, 317 protocol fee counters, 36 ERC-6909 balances, 2 operator flags. All 414 slot0 words read nonzero, as did 747 position words and 1,016 tick words, which confirms the derivation. The official endpoint answers only latest, so every batch of 18 reads was bracketed with eth_blockNumber; all 489 brackets had equal ends, between 52,276,229 and 52,276,658. rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31) returned the same word for all 8,781 items at the bracket block. rpc.hyperlend.finance (reth/v0.1.0-b92ad36) returned the same word for 8,761 items; one batch of 20 was lost to HTTP 429 refusals (227 refusals recorded and retried). No difference was found, so no neighbour re-read was needed. The last 10,000 blocks held only 4 Initialize logs (blocks 52,266,188 to 52,266,493), so the whole-history set was used to make the comparison meaningful. PoolManager native balance 0x9d908ef23bc0864f on all three. Files official_reads.json, replica_purroof.json, replica_hyperlend.json, slots.json.

cleared.check: L-995 base fee: whether any HyperEVM block after genesis had a base fee below the 100,000,000 wei level, which would let a legacy transaction with gas price 0 pass the standard EIP-1559 check.
cleared.result: eth_feeHistory over all 52,276,001 blocks from 0 to 52,276,000 (8 workers on rpc.purroofgroup.com f0cad31 and rpc.hyperlend.finance b92ad36, 387 HTTP 429 refusals retried) shows base fee 0 only in block 0 (genesis) and no block below 100,000,000 wei after it. Under the EIP-1559 rule a legacy or EIP-2930 transaction needs gas price at least the base fee, so a public transaction with gas price 0 would be invalid in every block. The base fees come from the validator's own headers, which nanoreth does not recompute (its parent base fee check is commented out, src/node/consensus/mod.rs:92-96), and the validator's admission rule itself is closed.

cleared.check: L-995 census: gas price 0 transactions in every block with a PoolManager log (2,405 blocks) and in 3,000 blocks drawn uniformly over the chain (seed 2026112623, range 1 to 52,276,000), grouped by decoded sender and target, with the official block of each read for comparison.
cleared.result: 1,579 gas price 0 transactions in 1,089 blocks, all of type 0, all at the start of their block. 45 senders: 0x2222...2222 (98, native HYPE credits), 42 addresses with prefix 0x20 (token system addresses), and two others: 0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24 (488, the USDC linked contract per spotMeta, a 2,175 byte proxy) and 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00 (191, no code, nonce 1,069,810), each calling USDC transfer to the other. None targets the PoolManager or carries its address in the first word. In each of the 5,405 blocks the replica's transaction count minus the official count of regular transactions equals the number of gas price 0 transactions (29,012 minus 27,433 = 1,579), no official regular transaction has gas price 0 or a fee cap of 0, and for 150 blocks the official eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber lists exactly the same senders, targets and selectors in the same order. Over the full history, the 2,642 ERC-20 Transfer logs with the PoolManager as source sit in 2,293 transactions, none with gas price 0. The PoolManager nonce is 1 on the official endpoint and on both replicas at latest, and nanoreth increments the sender nonce of system transactions (0x6b9e77... has nonce 2,399,458), so no transaction in history has run with the PoolManager as sender on either replica.

cleared.check: Whether the nanoreth rule that gas price 0 means system transaction can classify an EIP-1559, EIP-7702 or EIP-4844 transaction as a system transaction.
cleared.result: is_system_transaction tests tx.gas_price() == Some(0) (src/node/primitives/transaction.rs:182-184, src/node/evm/executor.rs:44-49). In alloy-consensus 2.5.0, the version in nanoreth's Cargo.lock, gas_price() returns None for EIP-1559, EIP-7702 and EIP-4844 transactions (src/transaction/eip1559.rs:174-176, eip7702.rs:162-164, eip4844.rs:488-490) and Some for legacy and EIP-2930. Only a type 0 or type 1 transaction with gas price 0 is taken as a system transaction. The rule is byte identical in the b92ad36 build behind rpc.hyperlend.finance; the f0cad31 build behind rpc.purroofgroup.com differs only in imports and trait plumbing.

cleared.check: Whether the zero BASEFEE that nanoreth gives to gas price 0 transactions (src/node/evm/mod.rs:135-145) or a gas price of 0 reaches any decision in src/.
cleared.result: src/ reads no BASEFEE, GASPRICE or ORIGIN. The only gas reads are GAS as the forwarded amount of three calls (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). A system transaction that calls a token runs the token's code, not the PoolManager's, and the PoolManager compares token balances only between sync and settle of one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and :349-365).

cleared.check: Past divergence between the closed validator and revm: the state patches nanoreth applies after particular transactions.
cleared.result: nanoreth drops the state changes of 19 listed transactions to match the validator (src/node/evm/patch.rs:7-27), all in blocks 1,467,569 to 1,531,366. The PoolManager was deployed at block 45,998,366 (binary search with eth_getCode on rpc.purroofgroup.com), so no patch touches it. The patch list cites a hyper-evm-sync commit that could not be fetched in this session (GitHub access refused), so the cause of those divergences is not confirmed.

leads.question: Repeat the 8,464 slot comparison between rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm and a nanoreth replica after the next block with PoolManager Swap or ModifyLiquidity activity, adding the bitmap words between each swap's start and end tick, and extend the gas price 0 census past the 5,405 blocks sampled here.
leads.why: This cycle found no difference, but the last 10,000 blocks held no swap, so a fault that only shows in a fresh swap or liquidity write was not exercised in the window.

leads.question: Is 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00 the registered AQAv2 treasury address of USDC (token 0), and does HyperCore refuse to register an address with code as treasury?
leads.why: 191 sampled system transactions move USDC in that address's name with no signature in the block. If an address with code could be registered, F-020 would apply to it.

leadResults.answer: Endpoints: rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, rpc.hypurrscan.io and hyperliquid-json-rpc.stakely.io answer 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet' (validator state; the official one ignores the block argument and answers latest, as its JSON-RPC page states); rpc.hyperlend.finance answers reth/v0.1.0-b92ad36 and rpc.purroofgroup.com reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 (nanoreth re-execution). Pinned by eth_blockNumber brackets between 52,276,229 and 52,276,658, all 8,464 PoolManager slots written over the whole history, the native balance and balanceOf of 316 currencies (WHYPE 0x5555...5555, USDC 0xb88339..., USDT0 0xb8ce59... among them) agree word for word between the official endpoint and f0cad31 (8,781 of 8,781) and b92ad36 (8,761 of 8,761, 20 lost to HTTP 429). No difference.

Range: whole history for base fees (52,276,001 blocks) and for PoolManager-sourced token transfers (2,642 logs); a census of 5,405 blocks for gas price 0 transactions. 1,579 gas price 0 transactions, all of type 0 and leading their block, all listed by the official endpoint as system transactions. Senders are 0x2222...2222, 42 addresses with prefix 0x20, the USDC linked contract 0x6b9e77... and 0xc20699... (no code); the last two are outside the expected set and match the AQAv2 rebalance between treasury and linked contract (F-020). No target is the PoolManager, no gas price 0 transaction moves a token out of the PoolManager, and the PoolManager nonce is 1 everywhere. The Hyperliquid documents do not state that a user transaction can never be mined with gas price 0; they state EIP-1559 is enabled and eth_gasPrice returns the base fee, and every block after genesis has base fee at least 100,000,000 wei, so the standard rule rejects it. The validator's admission code is closed and was not read.

The API reference lists authorizeAqav2Role with fields token and role ('technical' or 'treasury'), signed by the staking account, and the aligned quote assets page says the treasury deployer designates the treasury address and the linked contract rebalances with it. Neither page nor the Python SDK (no AQA code) names the action that sets the treasury address, which signature authorises a rebalance, or a rule against an address with code. On chain, rebalances appear as unsigned system transactions (official r=0, s=0) whose sender is 0xc20699... or the linked contract 0x6b9e77..., so the sender is the address HyperCore records, not a signer. F-020 stays plausible, high, operator.
